why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 only test values and behaviour that their lines require. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs `missing: none` from a regex, `'^#+\\s*'+f+'\\b'`, that only matches a heading starting with the function's name. "A section for every function" doesn't require that heading format. The regex is also broken: bash double quotes turn `\\s` into `\s` and `\\b` into `\b`, and in a JS string those become a literal "s" and a backspace character. So even `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` would not match, and Check 3 would fail a README that meets the line. That makes the PASS condition stricter than the words, and it isn't under Advisory.
